status: CONFIG ONLY, NOT YET COLLECTED. Created 2026-09-07 from pizza.json. Stop for review before collecting, per the method.
note: Method lives in .claude/skills/consensus-guide/SKILL.md. Read theScopeQuestion FIRST - it is the decision the whole guide rests on and it is settled with evidence, not preference. Then theCountingProblem, because half this scene is takeaway counters and a guide of sit-down rooms would be a different, smaller and less honest guide. Then theSourceMixVerdict.
theScopeQuestion:
RULING: THE GUIDE IS CARIBBEAN, WITH THE ISLANDS AS THE FACET AXIS. It is NOT a Jamaican guide. The evidence is one-sided and it came out of the SERP rather than out of preference.

THE DECIDING TEST WAS THE SEARCH ITSELF. The query 'best jamaican food london' returns NO Jamaican-specific editorial page from any masthead, blog or specialist. Its top organic results are Time Out's CARIBBEAN guide and The Infatuation's CARIBBEAN guide. The only Jamaican-TITLED results on that page were bestldn.com (a review-aggregating business directory, excluded below), a Caribbean catering company's own blog, and Yelp and Tripadvisor. A reader searching 'Jamaican' is already being served Caribbean pages, because that is what the publications wrote.

WHAT THE SERIOUS SOURCES ACTUALLY WRITE - all of them write 'Caribbean' and carry the islands INSIDE it:
  Time Out       '20 Best Caribbean Restaurants in London, FROM JAMAICAN TO TRINIDADIAN Cuisine', and its own intro promises 'the finest Jamaican, Guyanese, Trinidadian and Saint Lucian cuisine in the city'. It attributes an island to nearly every one of its 20.
  The Infatuation 'The 18 Best Caribbean Restaurants & Takeaways In London', spanning 'crunching Jamaican fried chicken, to Trinidadian roti, incredible Guyanese stews, and more'.
  Eater London    an entire map devoted to Indo-Caribbean roti, which OPENS by naming the problem: 'Caribbean takeouts and restaurants in London have become synonymous with Jamaican food over the years, owing to the island cuisine's dominance in U.K. Caribbean restaurants.' The map exists to correct that.
  The award       is the UK CARIBBEAN Food Awards. There is no Jamaican equivalent.

SO THE JAMAICAN DOMINANCE IS REAL AND IT IS A FINDING TO PRINT, NOT A TITLE TO ADOPT. Roughly twelve of Time Out's twenty are Jamaican or pan-Caribbean. The honest guide says so inside the article - with the island noted per venue - and then does the thing no competitor except a defunct Eater map has done, which is tell a reader where to get doubles, pepperpot and a Saint Lucian bake. Titling the guide 'Jamaican' would erase the four other traditions the sources themselves take trouble to name.

DO NOT REVISIT THIS WITHOUT NEW EVIDENCE. The test to re-run is the simple one: does any masthead publish a standalone 'best Jamaican restaurants in London' list. On 2026-09-07, none did.
theCountingProblem:
TAKEAWAY COUNTERS, BAKERIES AND MARKET STALLS ARE IN SCOPE. THE SOURCES SETTLED THIS, NOT US.

The Infatuation's guide is titled 'Caribbean Restaurants & TAKEAWAYS' and roughly twelve of its eighteen entries are takeaway-led - it prints the format per venue ('mostly takeaway-only but there are a few tables', 'takeaway with counter stalls', 'takeaway/delivery only'). Time Out's twenty include two bakeries (Rainbow Bakery, Healthy Eaters), a patty shop (Jamaica Patty Co) and a food-hall stall (Sweet Dee's Jerk, in Selfridges). James Dimitri's 39 include a bus cafe and a jerk pan in a park.

A SIT-DOWN-ONLY GUIDE WOULD CUT THE INFATUATION'S LIST ROUGHLY IN HALF and would remove almost every cheap entry in the topic. It would also be the exact failure the method already recorded on breakfast, where five mastheads agreed with each other and nothing below about £15 existed.

FOUR EDGE CASES TO RULE ON BEFORE COLLECTING, not during:
  1. HORIZON FOODS (Bull Lane, N18). Eater names it and says plainly it is 'not a shop per se' - a Trinidadian wholesale roti factory that sells to walk-ins at trade prices. A reader cannot eat there. RECOMMEND: out of the main ranking, worth a line in the format section.
  2. DELIVERY-ONLY KITCHENS. The Infatuation describes Chaconia as 'takeaway/delivery only' while Eater describes a Deptford High Street shop with a side warmer. One of the two is out of date. Resolve before printing either.
  3. EVENTS ARE NOT VENUES. DesignMyNight's list of 'venues' includes two recurring EVENTS - a House of Flavas x Windrush brunch and a Caribbean Night at Leonardo City. Drop both at extraction or they become permanently one-source phantom venues (trap 8 with a venue-shaped surface).
  4. THE HALL IS NOT THE TRADER. Brixton Village, Market Row and Pop Brixton are already recorded as venues in street-food.json and markets.json. SKILL.md section 6 is explicit: named traders only, never the hall. Do not record Brixton Village here, and do not let a trader inherit the hall's citations.
theOverlapFinding:
TRAP 13 CHECKED 2026-09-07. NO URL COLLISION: not one of the seed URLs in data/serp/caribbean.txt appears in street-food.json, markets.json, cheap-eats.json, general.json, late-night.json or any other consensus file. Safe to seed.

VENUE OVERLAP IS SMALL BUT REAL. Eight subjects are already recorded elsewhere:
  general.json      Tasty Jerk (The Infatuation), Jerk Yard (The Picky Glutton, Deptford)
  cheap-eats.json   Roti Stop (Time Out), Hut Negril (The Infatuation), Rudie's (Devour Tours)
  sunday-roast.json Buster Mantis - and it is RANKED, #14 in Time Out's Sunday lunch list, 'a ravishing Jamaican-inspired roast in Deptford'; Guanabana (The Infatuation)
  street-food.json  Brixton Village (Time Out, #3), Pop Brixton (DesignMyNight) - HALLS, not traders
  markets.json      Brixton Village x3 (Time Out, Lamplit London, Little Grey Box), 'Brixton Village and Market Row'

THE BRIXTON COLLISION IS NOT THE ONE THAT WAS EXPECTED. The brief anticipated a clash over Brixton Village and Pop Brixton TRADERS. There is none: both corpora recorded the HALL and no individual Caribbean trader inside either. So the collision risk runs the other way - a Caribbean pass that records Brixton Village as a venue would duplicate an existing record AND break the named-traders-only rule at the same time.

TRAP 7 IS THE LIVE RISK. Buster Mantis carries a Time Out Sunday-lunch RANK and Tasty Jerk, Roti Stop and Guanabana carry counts from other topics. None of those numbers may be printed on this page. evidence.json records `topics`; check topics.includes('caribbean') before printing any count or rank.

FALSE POSITIVES IN THE GREP - DO NOT PULL THESE IN. They matched on the word, not the food:
  ROTI KING (chains.json, cheap-eats.json) is MALAYSIAN roti canai, not Trinidadian roti. Londonist's roti guide makes the split explicit - 'Best for Malaysian roti: Roti King' against 'Best for Trinidadian roti: Roti Joupa'. This is the single easiest wrong merge in the topic.
  JAMAICA WINE HOUSE (historic-pubs.json) is a City of London pub named after the coffee trade. Not Caribbean.
  KRICKET (indian.json, general.json, activities.json) matched on 'Kricket'. Not Caribbean.
  'St Lucian rum' and 'St Lucia' (hot-chocolate.json) are quote text about chocolate, not venues.
  'rotisserie' (french.json) matched the substring 'roti'.

awardBodies.name: UK Caribbean Food Awards
awardBodies.verified: 2026-09-07 - THE AWARD IS REAL, JUDGED AND DATED. THE WEBSITE IS DEAD. Both halves of that matter.
awardBodies.note:
IT EXISTS AND IT IS THE ONLY JUDGED AWARD ANYWHERE FOR CARIBBEAN FOOD IN BRITAIN. Founded 2023 by Dawn Burton and Marsha Barnett (also founders of The Caribbean Food Collective), run with Deliveroo and KERB as category sponsors, ceremony at The Clapham Grand. Over twenty categories including Best Caribbean Restaurant, Best Caribbean Takeaway, Best Caribbean Bakery, Caribbean Street-Food Trader and Outstanding Caribbean Chef - a category list that maps unusually well onto theCountingProblem above.

JUDGED, ON THE EVIDENCE AVAILABLE. Country & Town House's report of the 2023 edition names six judges. NCASS names the 2024 Best Takeaway cook-off panel: Dawn Burton, Marsha Barnett, Jackson McLarty (founder of Black Eats LDN) and Oke Omoniyi. Soca News quotes the judges commending the 2024 winner. What is NOT published anywhere reachable is the full methodology - whether entry is by public nomination, whether there is a public vote stage, and what the judges scored. Record it as tier A but say in the config, not on the page, that the method is undisclosed.

KNOWN RESULTS:
  2023, 1st annual  Best Caribbean Restaurant: ROGER'S KITCHEN, London. Also London: Dees Imports (grocery), Essence of Cake (rum cake), Guava Kitchen (vegan). Media Personality: Andi Oliver. Lifetime Achievement: Rustie Lee.
  2024, 2nd annual, ceremony 8 December 2024  Best Caribbean Restaurant: LIMIN SOUTHBANK.
  2025, 3rd annual   NO PUBLISHED RESULTS FOUND. See knownGaps.
  2026, 4th annual   scheduled 23 November 2026 - AFTER this guide would publish. Do not write it as though it has happened.

TRAP 12 - IT IS UK-WIDE, NOT LONDON. The 2023 winners include Wakefield, Birmingham, Manchester and Croydon. Roughly five of fourteen 2023 winners are London. Scope every year before counting a single citation.

TRAP 2 - THE AWARD IS THE SOURCE, NOT THE OUTLET. Its results reached this pass through Country & Town House, NCASS, Soca News, London Daily News, News Shopper, Caterer & Licensee and thatsup.co.uk. Every one of those is relaying, not judging. File the citations under the award. Country & Town House is a tier-B masthead elsewhere on this site and must NOT also be counted as an independent Caribbean opinion on the strength of its awards write-up.

SEVERAL NON-RESTAURANT CATEGORIES MUST BE DROPPED at extraction: drinks (Negrill, Auntie Sam's Rum Tump), grocery (Dees Imports), cake (Essence of Cake), people (Andi Oliver, Rustie Lee, Chef Dexter Thomas), and Best African Eatery and Best Latin American Eatery, which are not Caribbean at all.

awardBodiesChecked: ukcaribbeanfoodawards.co.uk IS DOWN AND THAT IS THE BLOCKER ON TIER A. It returns Cloudflare error 526 (invalid origin SSL certificate) to WebFetch AND to the browser pane, 2026-09-07. Trap 6 was applied - /awards/, /awards/page/2/ and the www variant were all tried and all 526. Trap 14 was applied - the Wayback Machine's most recent capture (24 July 2024) is an UNBUILT WORDPRESS TEMPLATE reading 'Experience the Flavors of newsite'. So the awards have never had a working public results page; the live presence is Instagram (@ukcaribbeanfoodawards), Facebook and Eventbrite. DO NOT SEED THE DOMAIN - a dead origin records as a zero-venue source (trap 8). Someone has to either re-check the domain later or read the winners off Instagram by hand.
World Culinary Awards - NOT TIER A FOR THIS TOPIC. It publishes 'Jamaica's Best Restaurant', an award for restaurants IN Jamaica. Nothing to do with London.

National Restaurant Awards (nationalrestaurantawards.co.uk) - a general UK top-100 with no Caribbean category. Check whether any Caribbean venue places in the current year, but it is not a topic award.

Uber Eats Restaurant of the Year - a delivery platform's promotional prize decided on platform data and public voting, not a judged ranking. Its 2024 South England winner was a Jamaican restaurant, which is why it surfaces on this SERP. NOT tier A. Do not record it.

UK JERK FEST - NOT TIER A, BUT CHECK IT AGAIN BEFORE COLLECTING. A competition-led festival at Hackney Bridge, 25-26 July 2026, presented by Black Eats LDN and Grace Foods, founded by Jackson McLarty and intended to run annually. Eleven vendors competed. TWO OF ITS THREE CATEGORIES ARE PUBLIC VOTE ('Best Jerk in the UK', 'Jerk Innovation') and only 'Judges' Choice' is panel-selected, which is not enough to make it a judged ranking. It also covers ONE DISH, not restaurants. No results were published in anything this pass could reach. If the Judges' Choice winner is published somewhere, it is worth a single tier-A-adjacent citation for that venue and nothing more - do not record the public-vote categories at all.

THE FRAMING TO KEEP, FROM AN INSIDER. Jackson McLarty, founder of Black Eats LDN and a judge of the UK Caribbean Food Awards: 'Caribbean restaurants have historically been overlooked by Britain's most prestigious food institutions.' That is the reason this topic has almost no tier A, said by someone inside it, and it is attributable. If the guide needs to explain why there is little judged evidence, quote him rather than writing a weakness line.
Michelin - guide.michelin.com is on the permanent403 list in data/sources.json. No London Caribbean restaurant is expected to hold a star or Bib; check the Wikipedia substitute rather than assuming.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE. 20 venues, published 15 June 2026, by KESHIA SAKARAH (Contributor).
editorialLists.note:
THE BEST-SOURCED LIST IN THE TOPIC, and the byline is why. Keshia Sakarah is a Caribbean chef and food writer, not a generalist listicle writer, and the list attributes an ISLAND to nearly every venue - which is what makes the facet axis below buildable at all.

NOT RANKED. Numbered 1-20 but the intro presents a selection ('Featuring the finest Jamaican, Guyanese, Trinidadian and Saint Lucian cuisine in the city') with an at-a-glance block grouped by cuisine rather than an order. Trap 11 says Time Out's lists are OFTEN ranked and the label changes between them - re-read the caption before recording a single rank, but the reading here is unordered.

DECLARE THE INTEREST BEFORE PUBLISHING. Keshia Sakarah runs the Caribbean restaurant Antillean. Antillean is NOT on her Time Out list - which is the correct handling and worth noting - but it IS named by London x London. If both sources are counted, the guide should not present Antillean as though two unrelated voices backed it without someone checking that first.

NAMES: Paradise Cove, Buster Mantis, 2210 by NattyCanCook, Roti Joupa, All Roads, Sweet Dee's Jerk, Jam Delish, Veg & Tings, Umana Yana, Maureen's Brixton Kitchen, Dub Pan, Roti Stop, Limin, Healthy Eaters, Ma Petite Jamaica, Guanabana, Rainbow Bakery, Jamaica Patty Co, Trinidad Roti Shop, Peppers & Spice.

editorialLists.name: The Infatuation
editorialLists.ranked: RATED, NOT ORDERED - READ THE CAVEAT BELOW BEFORE RECORDING A RANK
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE AND VERY RECENT. 18 venues, published 28 August 2026, by Jake Missing and Heidi Lauth Beasley. It DOES carry a numeric rating against every venue.
editorialLists.note:
THE FORMAT SOURCE. It is the only list in the corpus that states per venue whether you sit down, stand at a counter or take it away - 'mostly takeaway-only but there are a few tables', 'takeaway with counter stalls', 'takeaway/delivery only', 'a handful of tables and some counter stalls'. That is the raw material for formatSection and for theCountingProblem, and no other source prints it.

IT IS RATED BUT ITS PAGE ORDER IS NOT THE RATING ORDER, AND THAT IS A TRAP. Every venue carries a score out of 10, but the page runs Tasty Jerk 9.1, then Fish Wings & Tings 8.4, then Maureen's 8.5 - the sequence goes DOWN then UP. So recording a rank from page position would be wrong. Either record the RATING as the source's judgement, or record no rank at all. Do not convert position into rank.

THE RATINGS, as read 2026-09-07: Tasty Jerk 9.1, Maureen's Brixton Kitchen 8.5, Fish Wings & Tings 8.4, JB's Soul Food 8.4, Ewarts Jerk 8.3, People's Choice 8.1, One Love Kitchen 8.1, Jay Dees Catering 8.0, Chaconia 8.0, Umana Yana 7.9, Jam Delish 7.9, Ochi Caribbean Takeaway 7.9, Peppers & Spice 7.8, Veg & Tings 7.8, Paradise Cove 7.6, Roti Joupa Finsbury Park 7.6, Limin Southbank 7.5, Tawa Roti 7.4.

AND HERE IS THE MOST INTERESTING THING IN THE WHOLE TOPIC. The Infatuation's clear number one is TASTY JERK at 9.1 - a takeaway - a full 0.6 clear of the next venue. The UK Caribbean Food Awards' Best Caribbean Restaurant is LIMIN SOUTHBANK, which The Infatuation rates 7.5, its second-LOWEST score. The judged award and the most recent critic disagree almost completely, and the disagreement runs along the takeaway-versus-dining-room line that theCountingProblem is about. Per SKILL.md that belongs in two sentences inside section 1, not a section of its own. NOTE ALSO: SKILL.md forbids publishing a numeric score per venue - that rule is about scores WE derive. The Infatuation's own published rating is a source fact and may be quoted as theirs.

NAMES: Tasty Jerk, Fish Wings & Tings, Maureen's Brixton Kitchen, JB's Soul Food, Ewarts Jerk, People's Choice, One Love Kitchen, Jay Dees Catering, Paradise Cove, Chaconia, Umana Yana, Jam Delish, Ochi Caribbean Takeaway, Peppers & Spice, Roti Joupa Finsbury Park, Veg & Tings, Tawa Roti, Limin Southbank.

editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE via the browser (403s WebFetch). 10 venues, written by Ellie Donnell, updated 22 August 2025.

403s the fetcher; read it in the browser. SCOPE ERROR IN ITS OWN LIST: it includes AREPA & CO, which is VENEZUELAN. Arepas are not Caribbean-island cooking and no other source names it. editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE via the browser (403s WebFetch). 8 venues. NO BYLINE AND NO DATE FOUND on the page.

The thinnest tier-B source here and the only one with no byline. It is in because The Handbook is already registered tier B and the eight names are real and specific, but it adds only one name nobody else has.

editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE. Only 5 venues, by Rob Crossan, 4 June 2024.
editorialLists.note:
SMALL AND TWO YEARS OLD, but a named writer and five specific rooms, and it is the only masthead naming Bluejay Cafe in South Norwood. Worth having for breadth, not for weight.

editorialLists.name: DesignMyNight
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE and, unusually for this domain, a genuine editorial list with prose per venue rather than a directory. By Scarlett Welch (Editor), updated 7 July 2026.
editorialLists.note:
DesignMyNight returned pure chrome twice in bars.json and is flagged in wine-bars.json as untrustworthy. On THIS topic it behaves: nine real venues with real descriptions. It is also the source that reaches furthest into the new, expensive end - UNDR, Sama Bankside, The Good Front Room and Cocos Dining Experiences appear on almost no other list.

DROP THE TWO EVENTS. Its list mixes in a House of Flavas x Windrush brunch and a Caribbean Night at Leonardo City. Those are events, not venues. See theCountingProblem item 3.

NAMES: UNDR, Sama Bankside, Cottons Shoreditch, Rudie's Shoreditch, Limin Southbank, Cocos Dining Experiences, Market Place Vauxhall, 2210 by NattyCanCook, The Good Front Room.

editorialLists.name: Eater London
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE BUT THE PUBLICATION IS DEFUNCT. The map is dated 11 November 2022 and the site's own last post is 'Farewell, Eater London', 14 February 2023. Blocked to WebFetch; read in the browser pane.
editorialLists.note:
THE MOST IMPORTANT SINGLE SOURCE IN THIS TOPIC DESPITE BEING FOUR YEARS OLD, because it is the ONLY publication anywhere that treats Indo-Caribbean, Trinidadian and Guyanese food as a subject in its own right. Written by RIAZ PHILLIPS, author of 'Belly Full: Caribbean Food in the UK'. Without it the guide has almost no Guyanese coverage and the island axis collapses back into Jamaican.

ONE VOICE, THREE PLATFORMS - MERGE BY HAND. Riaz Phillips also writes a Caribbean guide on trippin.world AND a Time Out blog post ('Author of Belly Full shares his favourite London spots'). hostOf() cannot see that these are one person, exactly as it could not see @dejashu across YouTube and TikTok. Counting them separately would let one writer vote three times, and the Time Out one would additionally double-count a masthead already in this corpus.

STALENESS IS A REAL RISK, not a formality. Four years is long enough for a takeaway to close. Check every one is trading before printing it.

TRAP 12 AT THE SMALL END: it calls Roti Masters 'Croydon's Roti Masters' and then prints a SUTTON SM1 address. Both are Greater London, so it stays in, but do not repeat the Croydon claim.

NAMES: Roti Kitchen (West Ealing), Roti Rolls Hut Taste (Ealing), Trinidad Roti Shop (Craven Park), Roti Joupa (Shepherd's Bush), Roti Masters (Sutton), Umana Yana (Herne Hill), Horizon Foods (N18 - see theCountingProblem), Roti Stop Ltd (Stamford Hill), Roti Island (South Norwood), Chaconia (Deptford).

editorialLists.name: The Glossary
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE via the browser (403s WebFetch). 9 venues, by Luciana Bellini.
editorialLists.note:
Already registered tier C. Named writer, real names, no furniture. It is the only source besides The Handbook to name Roger's Kitchen - which matters, because Roger's Kitchen won the award's first Best Caribbean Restaurant and is otherwise almost invisible in the editorial tier. Also the only source naming Marvee's Food Shop.

editorialLists.name: James Dimitri
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - PASSED THE BLOG-VS-SEO-FARM TEST ON EVERY POINT. Named writer, dated 27 August 2026, sustained first person ('I always get', 'I've been back twice now'), his own photography, British spellings throughout, and honest negative judgements rather than uniform praise.
editorialLists.note:
THE SINGLE BIGGEST AND BEST INDEPENDENT SOURCE IN THE TOPIC, and the reason data/serp exists. 39 venues against Time Out's 20 - this is the mayfairfoodie.com and blog.resy.com pattern repeating exactly.

IT IS ALSO THE ONLY SOURCE THAT REACHES THE BOTTOM OF THE SCENE. Roughly twenty of its names appear on NO other list found in this pass: Crystal Caterers, New Tings, Sunvalley Jerk, Smokey Jerkey, Jerk in Da Park, Survivor, Double Knot, Moto Roti, White Men Can't Jerk, Cool Runnings Jerk Centre, Bokit'la, Cafe Caribbean, Swift Caribbean Delights, Rainbow Cook Out, Mum's Caribbean Takeaway, Jeff the Chef, Heart & Soul Caribbean Food, Richie's, Lickle D, the Peckham Bus Garage Bus Cafe, Jamaican Tuck Shop, True Flavours, DJ's Caribbean Cuisine, Hot Grubz. Several of those are the weekend pans and stalls that decide whether this guide is honest about the scene or not.

HANDLING: it names 'Roti Stop Ltd' (Eater's spelling) and 'Maureen's' (short form) and lists both 'Bus Cafe' and 'Peckham Bus Garage Bus Cafe', which look like one subject under two names. Alias all three before recording. 'Bokit'la' carries an apostrophe - decode entities first (trap 9).

editorialLists.name: London x London
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. 14 venues, by Lauren Kendrick (Features Editor), 14 August 2023, updated 21 August 2023. THREE YEARS OLD.
editorialLists.note:
BORDERLINE-IN, and the reason is worth recording so the next pass does not re-argue it. AGAINST: no first-person visit narrative and no original photography - it runs embedded Instagram posts instead, which is the compiled-listicle shape. FOR: a named staff writer with a masthead title, British spellings, fourteen specific and correct London venues, and it is already registered tier C in data/sources.json.

IT IS IN because the independent tier on this topic is thin and because it names four venues nobody else does - Antillean, PandaBerry, Caribbean-Kitchen (Hackney) and The Rum Kitchen. If a later pass finds it aggregating rather than visiting, drop it and record here that it was dropped.

SEE THE TIME OUT ENTRY on Antillean: Time Out's writer owns it, and this is the only list that names it.

NAMES: Antillean, Limin, Negril, Rudie's, PandaBerry, Chaconia, Caribbean-Kitchen, Cottons, Buster Mantis, Fish Wings and Tings, Ma Petite Jamaica, Danclair's Kitchen, Guanabana, The Rum Kitchen.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE ITS CARIBBEAN PAGE. /caribbean-fine-dining-london/. Parent business is PS London, a LUXURY CONCIERGE that monetises restaurant bookings - the page is wrapped in 'Secure Your Table' and 'Speak to the Team' calls to action and membership plans. Byline is 'Charlotte H.' over a 'P.S. London Editorial Team' house organ. No original photography at all; the image slots are placeholder SVGs. Uniformly glowing, no critical line anywhere.
assessedAndExcluded.flagForAHuman: THIS DOMAIN IS ALREADY REGISTERED TIER C IN data/sources.json. Same shape as theworkingline.com on halal - a domain counted elsewhere on the site whose page on THIS topic fails the README's test on three named tells at once (parent business is not food, no visit evidence, booking monetisation). This pass did not change sources.json; that is a separate decision.
assessedAndExcluded.butKeepTheseNames: Its list is the only place this pass found RapChar (Brixton), Hoodwood (Stoke Newington), OMI Lounge and Ayanna's. It also names The Good Front Room and 2210 by NattyCanCook, which DesignMyNight independently backs. Do not count the source - but these are real rooms and a later pass should look for a countable source that names them.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE. 'The 5 Best Jamaican Restaurants in London'. No byline, no publication date (the footer's '© 2026' is a template placeholder), no visit evidence, no original photography. It is a business-directory platform and it says so - the venues are 'ranked by review aggregation', which is Tripadvisor's method wearing an editorial headline. Templated FAQ block and repetitive category linking. This is the only Jamaican-titled result that ranks, which makes excluding it more important, not less: it would otherwise be the sole evidence for a Jamaican-titled guide.

EXCLUDE. 'Best Caribbean Food in London - Top 10 Flavourful Spots'. It has a byline (Isla Rose) but the bio is 'sharing delicious RECIPES & kitchen inspiration from London' - it is a recipe site, not a dining publication. No date, no visit accounts, all images sourced externally, and the list leans on chains (Turtle Bay, Cottons, The Rum Kitchen). Fails on evidence-of-visit.

EXCLUDE - TIER F. 'Best Jamaican food in London', published on the blog of Aunty Madge Caribbean Cuisine, a Caribbean CATERING BUSINESS. A food business ranking the field it competes in is the venue's own marketing, the same call made on humblegrape.co.uk in wine-bars.json. Never count it.

NOT A SOURCE, BUT DO NOT LOSE IT. It is a DIRECTORY, not an editorial list: 538 user- and business-submitted listings including 263 tagged Caribbean, with 'Submit a Listing', paid 'Services' and 'Client Feedback' pages. Same call as dinehalal.uk on halal - a filterable database is not an opinion and must not be counted as one.
assessedAndExcluded.whyItStillMatters: Its founder Jackson McLarty is a NAMED JUDGE of the UK Caribbean Food Awards, so it is credible even though it is not countable. It also carries an 'Approved by Black Eats' filter of 52 venues described as 'our tried and tested recommendations' - which, unlike the other 486, may be a genuine editorial selection. WORTH A HUMAN CALL: read that subset and decide whether it is an editorial list under a directory's clothes. It is the closest thing found to a Black British food specialist with London-wide coverage, and this topic cannot afford to lose one lightly.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: LEFT OUT ON STALENESS, NOT ON QUALITY. 'Where To Eat London's Best Rotis' by Helen Graves is real editorial from a real masthead - but it is dated 2 OCTOBER 2018 and names only three venues. Eight years is too old to seed. Londonist is on the permanent403 list in data/sources.json and reads fine in the browser pane, so if a later pass finds a current Londonist Caribbean guide, take it.
assessedAndExcluded.butRecordThisFinding: The page is the cleanest published evidence for the Roti King trap in theOverlapFinding - it splits its own three picks as 'Best for MALAYSIAN roti: Roti King', 'Best for TRINIDADIAN roti: Roti Joupa', 'Best for GUYANESE roti: Umana Yana'. Keep the finding, not the citation.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE. 'We went to the best Caribbean restaurant in London' is a national tabloid's write-up of the award winner - trap 2 syndication. The award is the source. Same treatment for newsshopper.co.uk, londondaily.news, catererlicensee.com and thatsup.co.uk (the last already on the permanent403 and excluded lists).

NOT SEEDABLE AS A LIST, BUT IT IS THE COMMUNITY MASTHEAD THIS TOPIC WAS SUPPOSED TO HAVE. The Voice is Britain's Black newspaper, it has a standing Food section (/section/lifestyle/food/), and it covers London Caribbean restaurants continuously - Jam Delish, doubles in London, Bajan pop-ups, Jamaican Independence events, single-venue features. WHAT IT DOES NOT PUBLISH, on the evidence of this pass, is a 'best Caribbean restaurants in London' ROUND-UP, which is the shape this method counts. Single-venue features are not a list and cannot be recorded as one.
assessedAndExcluded.andBeCarefulHere: ITS CARIBBEAN AWARDS AND JERK FEST PIECES SIT IN THE /sponsored-2/ PATH AND ARE MARKED SPONSORED. Advertorial on a real masthead is still advertorial - it is tier F wearing a newspaper's masthead, the same call made on hosted creator content in SKILL.md. Never count a /sponsored-2/ URL. Its ordinary news and lifestyle coverage is a different matter.
assessedAndExcluded.whatToDoNext: WORTH A HUMAN TEN MINUTES BEFORE COLLECTION, because it would change the shape of this corpus more than anything else available: read /section/lifestyle/food/ and establish whether any round-up exists. If one does, it is a tier-B community masthead and the single most valuable addition to the topic.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: NOT COUNTED THIS PASS, BUT THE BEST UNEXPLORED LEAD IN THE TOPIC. Soca News is a genuine Caribbean-diaspora publication with named writers (Mia Anthony), covering carnival, music and a Food & Drink section. The page found is award reporting, which is trap 2 and not countable. NOBODY CHECKED whether it publishes its own London restaurant guides. If it does, it is exactly the community-publication voice this topic is short of. Worth ten minutes before collection.

DO NOT SEED SEPARATELY. 'Caribbean Food Spots in London with Riaz Philips' is the SAME WRITER as the Eater map already in the corpus. One creator, three platforms (Eater, trippin.world, a Time Out blog post) - merge by hand or he votes three times. If Eater's map is ever dropped for staleness, this is the live replacement for that voice, not an addition to it.

excludeOnSight: tripadvisor.co.uk and tripadvisor.com - ranked twice on the first SERP. User-review aggregation, already excluded globally.
thefork.co.uk / thefork.com - booking platform directory, ranked on all three SERPs.
yelp.com - already excluded globally; ranked three times on the Jamaican query.
opentable.co.uk - already excluded; it took the paid slot at the top of the main SERP.
thatsup.co.uk - already on the permanent403 and excluded lists.
rotimasters.com, trinirotishop.com - venues' own sites. Tier F, weight 0, excluded at collection.
goodtoorder.com - untested, appeared once. Assume excluded unless a read finds a named writer and evidence of a visit.
theSourceMixVerdict:
THE TOPIC IS VIABLE. THE SOURCE-MIX FLOOR IS NOT REACHABLE IN THIS ENVIRONMENT. Those are two different statements and both are true.

WHY IT IS VIABLE, which was the open question going in: ELEVEN countable sources across ELEVEN distinct domains, and they are not all one shape. ONE tier A (a real judged award), SEVEN tier B, THREE tier C. Ten of the eleven are seedable list URLs in data/serp/caribbean.txt; the eleventh is the award, whose own website is dead. The two biggest lists in the topic - Time Out's 20 and James Dimitri's 39 - are written by a Caribbean chef and an independent blogger respectively, not by generalists recycling each other. That is a better-founded corpus than halal managed (one masthead, seven blogs, no award) and it is enough to measure a consensus.

WHAT THE FLOOR REQUIRES AND WHAT IS MISSING. A judged award exists, so scripts/audit-source-mix.mjs wants TWO independent social voices rather than three. Available: ZERO of 2.
  TIER D (video) - blocked because APIFY_TOKEN is not set. THIS IS THE EXPENSIVE LOSS ON THIS TOPIC SPECIFICALLY. Caribbean food in London is one of the most heavily filmed subjects on YouTube and TikTok in this city - jerk pans, patty runs, roti shops and 'best Caribbean takeaway' rankings are a whole genre, and the creators making them are largely the community the food belongs to. Losing tier D here does not just thin a count, it removes the voices closest to the subject and leaves the corpus 80% masthead. Setting the token is the single largest available win on this topic.
  TIER E (community) - Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser pane. Not fixable from here. Only route is Rob pasting thread URLs by hand.

AND THE SHAPE PROBLEM NO SCRIPT WILL CATCH. Seven of eleven sources are tier B mastheads. audit-source-mix flags a corpus that is over 70% SOCIAL; it does not flag one that is 64% masthead. The mastheads also converge hard - Limin appears on seven of the ten lists, Buster Mantis on six, Jam Delish on five - so the top of the ranking will be decided by publications that read each other. The two sources that break that pattern are James Dimitri (24 names nobody else has) and Eater (the entire Guyanese and Indo-Caribbean side of the topic), and one of those is four years old and defunct.

RECOMMENDATION: set APIFY_TOKEN and run the video tier BEFORE collecting rather than after. If that is not possible, this is a topic to ASK about rather than to publish thin - per ask-dont-publish-gaps, the gap goes to Rob, never onto the page.

facetAxis.note:
THE AXIS IS THE ISLAND, AND EVERY SERIOUS SOURCE ALREADY USES IT. Time Out attributes an island to nearly all 20 of its venues and puts two of them in its title. The Infatuation's scope line is island-by-island. Eater's whole map is Indo-Caribbean. Londonist splits its three roti picks as Malaysian, Trinidadian and Guyanese. It is also the only axis that answers a real question - a reader who wants doubles cannot get them at a jerk shop, and nothing on a menu tells them which is which.

WHY NOT AREA, WHICH WAS THE OTHER CANDIDATE: because the geography and the island are THE SAME AXIS, and the island one is the one the reader can act on. The addresses in the corpus fall out like this - the Trinidadian and Guyanese roti shops cluster in WEST (Ealing, Shepherd's Bush) and NORTH (Craven Park, Stamford Hill, Finsbury Park, Edmonton) and OUTER SOUTH-EAST (Croydon, South Norwood, Herne Hill), while Brixton is overwhelmingly the JAMAICAN centre and Deptford and Peckham are Jamaican-led too. Splitting by area would print the island split twice under a worse label and would bury the fact that Brixton, the area everyone names, is not where the roti is. AREA BECOMES A CROSS-REFERENCE SECTION - 'Where to eat by neighbourhood', one line per venue - alongside Cheapest and Quickest. That is a section, not an axis.

DO NOT ADD A VALUE THE CORPUS CANNOT FILL. Cuban is in the list because London has the rooms, not because a source ranks them; if collection turns up fewer than three, cut it rather than printing a two-venue section.

values.label: Jamaican
values.describeAs: jerk chicken off a smoking oil-drum pan, curry goat, ackee and saltfish, patties and hard-dough bread

values.label: Trinidadian
values.describeAs: doubles - two soft fried bara breads folded round curried chickpeas - and buss-up-shut roti torn into curry

values.label: Guyanese
values.describeAs: pepperpot, the slow black stew made with cassareep, and cassava pone for afters

values.label: Bajan and Saint Lucian
values.describeAs: fried fish and cou-cou, salt bread and green fig, from the Eastern Caribbean

values.label: Pan-Caribbean
values.describeAs: kitchens that cook across the islands rather than from one, usually the newer dining rooms

values.label: Cuban
values.describeAs: ropa vieja and moros y cristianos, rice and black beans, from the Spanish-speaking Caribbean

facetAxis.checkBeforePrinting: CUBAN AND BAJAN/SAINT LUCIAN ARE THE THIN ONES. This pass found exactly one Saint Lucian venue named by any source (Rainbow Bakery, via Time Out) and ZERO Cuban venues on any Caribbean list - the Cuban rooms in London are bars and sell themselves as bars, which is why no food guide names them. Guyanese rests almost entirely on Eater's four-year-old map. Verify against the collected corpus before printing any of the three as a section.

formatSection.title: The ones that are only open some of the time
formatSection.note:
THE SECTION NOBODY ELSE PRINTS, AND ON THIS TOPIC IT IS THE FACT THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES THE TRIP. A large share of the best-regarded Caribbean cooking in London does not run a restaurant week. It runs a takeaway counter that sells out, a stall that trades three days, a jerk pan that appears at a weekend, or a kitchen inside somebody else's building. Turning up on the wrong day is the standard way a reader is let down here, and not one source in this corpus prints opening days as a fact you can act on - The Infatuation gets closest, and it prints the FORMAT (sit-down, counter, takeaway) rather than the DAYS.

THE FORMAT HALF IS ALREADY VERIFIED and can be built from the corpus today. The Infatuation states it per venue in its own words: Jay Dees Catering 'takeaway only'; Chaconia 'takeaway/delivery only'; Maureen's Brixton Kitchen 'mostly takeaway-only but there are a few tables'; Roti Joupa Finsbury Park 'takeaway with counter stalls'; Tawa Roti 'mostly takeaway with perching stalls'; Veg & Tings 'a handful of tables and some counter stalls'. Time Out adds the food-hall stall (Sweet Dee's Jerk, in Selfridges) and the bakeries (Rainbow Bakery, Healthy Eaters). Eater adds the one that is not a shop at all - Horizon Foods, 'not a shop per se', a roti factory that sells to walk-ins.

THE DAYS-AND-HOURS HALF IS VERIFIED TOO, AND EXACTLY ONE SOURCE CARRIES IT. Checked 2026-09-07 against both candidates: The Infatuation, despite printing the format per venue, publishes NO opening days, hours or sell-out information for any of its 18. James Dimitri publishes it repeatedly, in his own words:
  Maureen's, Brixton          'Every Tuesday-Saturday' - closed Sunday and Monday
  Hot Grubz, Park Royal       'Monday-Friday lunchtimes only'
  Cafe Caribbean, Spitalfields 'serving lunch during the week to the office crowd'
  Jay Dees, Notting Hill      'If you go just before midday you can get your jerk chicken straight off the drum' and 'Don't come too late in the day because they'll run out of half of the menu'
  Mum's Caribbean Takeaway    'Go earlier in the day as they have run out of half the menu by evening'
  Sunvalley Jerk, Borough     'serving food outside of a truck in Tabard Street Food Market'
  Bokit'la, Oval              'A French Caribbean food truck', variable market pitches
  Peppers & Spice, Dalston    'it's takeaway only and there isn't really anywhere comfortable nearby to enjoy your food'
SO THE SECTION IS BUILDABLE, and the reason it is buildable is the reason it is worth printing: the independent blogger did the legwork the seven mastheads did not. That asymmetry IS the section's justification.

BUT DO NOT REST THE WHOLE SECTION ON ONE SOURCE. Confirm each venue's days against its own site or listing at collection, because a wrong day costs the reader the trip - the same class of error as a dead booking link. NEVER ESTIMATE ONE. Where the days cannot be confirmed, print the format fact (counter, stall, takeaway-only) WITHOUT the days rather than guessing, and ask rather than publishing the gap.

WHY NOT THE OTHER CANDIDATES. CASH-ONLY was considered and rejected, and the evidence for rejecting it is good: James Dimitri writes of Maureen's 'SURPRISINGLY it's not cash only, they do take card payments too', which tells you cash-only is an assumption people carry about this scene rather than a documented fact about it. Building a section on an assumption is how a guide gets something wrong about a community's restaurants, and it is unpublished everywhere the fetcher can reach. TAKEAWAY-ONLY alone is too narrow - The Infatuation already prints it, so it is not a section no competitor has. MARKET-STALL-VERSUS-RESTAURANT is the same fact from a worse angle and it collides with the food-halls section every guide on this site already runs. Opening days is the only candidate that is a decision the reader actually makes, is verifiable, and is printed by nobody else.

knownGaps: A JUDGED AWARD EXISTS - the UK Caribbean Food Awards, founded 2023, over twenty categories, named judges, ceremony at The Clapham Grand. Its presence sets the source-mix floor at TWO social voices rather than three. BUT ITS WEBSITE IS DEAD: ukcaribbeanfoodawards.co.uk returns Cloudflare 526 to the fetcher and the browser alike, and the most recent Wayback capture (July 2024) is an unbuilt WordPress template. Winners are only readable through outlets reporting them, which is trap 2 - the award is the source and the outlet is not.

NO 2025 (3rd annual) RESULTS FOUND ANYWHERE. 2023 and 2024 winners are both confirmed through reporting; the 3rd edition is not. The 4th annual is scheduled for 23 NOVEMBER 2026, which is AFTER this guide would publish - do not write about it as though it has happened. Someone should read @ukcaribbeanfoodawards on Instagram for the 2025 list, or ask.

TIER D (video) needs APIFY_TOKEN, NOT SET, AND THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE MISSING TIER ON ANY TOPIC SO FAR. Caribbean food in London is filmed constantly - jerk pan visits, patty rankings, roti shop tours are a whole YouTube and TikTok genre, and the creators are largely from the community whose food it is. Losing tier D leaves this corpus 70% masthead on a subject the mastheads cover thinly. Fix before collecting, not after.
TIER E (community) cannot be collected here - Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser pane. Only fix is Rob pasting thread URLs by hand.

SEVEN OF ELEVEN SOURCES ARE TIER B MASTHEADS and they converge hard - Limin appears on seven lists, Buster Mantis on six, Jam Delish on five. No script flags a masthead-heavy corpus; audit-source-mix only flags social over 70%.

THE GUYANESE AND INDO-CARIBBEAN SIDE OF THE TOPIC RESTS ON ONE FOUR-YEAR-OLD SOURCE from a publication that has since closed. If Eater's 2022 map is dropped for staleness, the guide loses Guyanese food almost entirely. Riaz Phillips' trippin.world guide is the same voice and would replace it, not supplement it.

OPENING DAYS AND SELL-OUT TIMES ARE PUBLISHED BY EXACTLY ONE SOURCE - James Dimitri, the independent blog. All seven mastheads print none, including The Infatuation, which prints the format but never the hours. formatSection is buildable on that one source but should not REST on it; confirm each venue's days at collection.

SECTION 1 OF THE ARTICLE SHAPE HAS SOMETHING TO LEAD WITH, which is not true of every topic. Two published orderings exist: the UK Caribbean Food Awards' Best Caribbean Restaurant (Roger's Kitchen 2023, Limin Southbank 2024) and The Infatuation's per-venue ratings (Tasty Jerk 9.1 down to Tawa Roti 7.4). They disagree sharply - see the Infatuation entry. Do NOT sort section 1 by citation count; lead with what won.

THE COMMUNITY PUBLICATIONS EXIST AND NONE OF THEM PUBLISHES A ROUND-UP THIS METHOD CAN COUNT. Two were found and both are real: THE VOICE (voice-online.co.uk), Britain's Black newspaper, with a standing Food section and continuous London Caribbean coverage; and SOCA NEWS (socanews.com), a Caribbean-diaspora publication with named writers and a Food & Drink section. Both write single-venue features and event coverage; neither was found to publish a 'best Caribbean restaurants in London' list. That is the sourcing problem in this topic stated precisely - the community press covers this food constantly and does not rank it, while the mastheads rank it and cover it thinly. Both are worth a human ten minutes before collection; a round-up on either would be the most valuable single addition available.
THE VOICE'S CARIBBEAN AWARDS AND JERK FEST ARTICLES ARE SPONSORED CONTENT, in the /sponsored-2/ path. Never count a sponsored URL, on any masthead.
THE 'APPROVED BY BLACK EATS' SUBSET (52 venues) inside blackeatsldn.com's directory is undecided on purpose. The directory is not a source; that curated subset might be one. A human should look.

Per SKILL.md and the no-weakness-lines rule: NONE of the above may be printed in the article. It lives here. If a gap is big enough that the guide would mislead without it, ask Rob or collect more - never print it.
openVenueQuestions: ROTI KING IS NOT CARIBBEAN AND IT IS ALREADY IN TWO CORPORA. It is recorded in chains.json and cheap-eats.json for MALAYSIAN roti canai. Londonist splits its own three picks as 'Best for Malaysian roti: Roti King' against 'Best for Trinidadian roti: Roti Joupa'. Any extractor matching on 'roti' will pull it in. Do not let it happen.

NEGRIL, HUT NEGRIL AND NEGRILL - THREE NAMES, AND POSSIBLY THREE DIFFERENT SUBJECTS. 'Negril' (Brixton Hill) is named by London x London and The Glossary. 'Hut Negril' is already recorded in cheap-eats.json from The Infatuation. 'Negrill' won the UK Caribbean Food Awards 2023 category for Caribbean NON-ALCOHOLIC DRINK, which is a product, not a restaurant. Do not merge any of these without checking. A wrong merge here would hand a Brixton restaurant a drinks award.

ROTI JOUPA HAS AT LEAST TWO BRANCHES AND SOURCES NAME DIFFERENT ONES - Eater names Shepherd's Bush (Goldhawk Road), The Infatuation names Finsbury Park, Time Out names it unqualified. Branches per chains.json, and decide the canonical name a reader books under (trap 17).

MAUREEN'S - three spellings across three sources: 'Maureen's Brixton Kitchen' (Time Out, The Infatuation), 'Maureen's Kitchen' (The Handbook), 'Maureen's' (James Dimitri). One venue. Alias before recording or it splits three ways.
MA PETITE JAMAICA is spelled 'Ma Petite JamaicaN' by The Handbook. Alias. It is also multi-branch (Camden and Shoreditch).

ROGER'S KITCHEN vs ROGERS KITCHEN - The Glossary and The Handbook print the apostrophe, the award reporting does not. This is the 2023 Best Caribbean Restaurant winner, so getting it wrong splits the topic's only tier-A restaurant citation off from its editorial ones.

LIMIN - four spellings: 'Limin' (Time Out, The Glossary, London x London), 'Limin Southbank' (The Infatuation, The Handbook, DesignMyNight, the award), 'LIMIN SOUTHBANK', 'Limin South Bank' (SquareMeal). It is the most-cited venue in the topic AND the 2024 award winner, so this is the alias that matters most.
'BUS CAFE' AND 'PECKHAM BUS GARAGE BUS CAFE' both appear in James Dimitri's own list. Probably one subject named twice. Confirm rather than assume - a wrong merge is invisible.
'ROTI STOP' (Time Out, Luxury London, already in cheap-eats.json) and 'ROTI STOP LTD' (Eater, James Dimitri) are one venue in Stamford Hill. Alias.

AREPA & CO IS VENEZUELAN and appears only on SquareMeal's Caribbean list. Drop it. GUANABANA is the softer version of the same question - Time Out calls it 'Pan-South American/Caribbean' and it is already recorded in sunday-roast.json. Decide whether pan-Latin kitchens are in scope at all, and apply the ruling to both.
HORIZON FOODS is a wholesale roti factory, not a restaurant - Eater's own words are 'not a shop per se'. Decide whether it belongs in the guide at all before it acquires a citation.

CHACONIA - The Infatuation (Aug 2026) says 'takeaway/delivery only'; Eater (2022) describes a Deptford High Street shop with a warmer and a counter. One of these is out of date. Check before printing either.

BUSTER MANTIS CARRIES A TIME OUT SUNDAY-LUNCH RANK (#14) IN sunday-roast.json. Trap 7: that rank and that count must never appear on this page. It is named by six Caribbean sources and will rank high here on its own evidence.

COTTONS, RUDIE'S, TURTLE BAY AND THE RUM KITCHEN ARE MULTI-BRANCH CHAINS and sources name them inconsistently ('Cottons' vs 'Cottons Shoreditch', 'Rudie's' vs 'Rudie's Shoreditch'). Chain handling per chains.json. Turtle Bay tops the SERP's local pack and appears on no serious editorial list except the excluded recipe blog - worth saying so rather than letting a reader assume it was missed.

ANTILLEAN IS NAMED BY ONE SOURCE ONLY (London x London), AND TIME OUT'S CARIBBEAN WRITER OWNS IT. Keshia Sakarah correctly kept it off her own Time Out list. Nothing improper has happened - but if the guide prints Antillean, someone should know the connection first.
ROTI MASTERS is called 'Croydon's Roti Masters' by Eater and given a SUTTON address. Both are Greater London so it stays in; do not repeat the Croydon claim.
TASTY JERK AND JERK YARD are both already in general.json - Tasty Jerk from The Infatuation, Jerk Yard from The Picky Glutton, both Deptford-adjacent. Different venues, similar names, do not merge.

BRIXTON VILLAGE, MARKET ROW AND POP BRIXTON are recorded as venues in markets.json and street-food.json. Do not record any of them here. If a Caribbean trader inside one is named by a source, record the TRADER.

Any wording in this file saying tier D is blocked because APIFY_TOKEN is unset is WRONG, on three counts, each verified: (1) APIFY_TOKEN IS set, 46 chars in .env.local - a script reading process.env without loading that file sees nothing, which is how the belief started; (2) the tier-D scripts do not use Apify at all - scripts/video-research.mjs shells out to yt-dlp and scripts/video-pass.mjs fetches youtube.com watch pages, and no script in scripts/ references APIFY_TOKEN; (3) yt-dlp is installed at the path video-research.mjs hardcodes, and a live search returned three real London videos in seconds. TIER D IS COLLECTABLE NOW, AT NO COST. Collect it before treating any source-mix verdict in this file as final. Tier E (Reddit) remains genuinely unreachable from this environment.
